subproblem.title: Hausdorff measure scaling under the blow-up map
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, x ∈ ℝ^P, r ∈ ℝ with r > 0, and S ⊆ ℝ^P an arbitrary (not necessarily measurable) set. Let η_{x,r}(y) := r⁻¹(y − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap x r) and Hⁿ := μHE[n] (Mathlib's normalized n-dimensional Euclidean Hausdorff measure). Then Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(S)) = r^{−n}·Hⁿ(S) in [0, ∞], the factor r^{−n} being written ENNReal.ofReal (r⁻¹ ^ n).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (x : Euclid P) (r : ℝ) (S : Set (Euclid P)), 0 < r → μHE[n] (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r '' S) = ENNReal.ofReal (r⁻¹ ^ n) * μHE[n] S
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Lemma A, step A4 (“η_λ is the translation y ↦ y − x (an isometry, Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image) followed by the dilation by λ⁻¹, so Hⁿ(η_λ(S)) = λ^{−n}Hⁿ(S) for every S”). This is the scaling used in Simon Ch. 3, proof of Theorem 1.6 “⇒”, where the integral over η_{x,λ}(M ∖ N_j) is bounded by sup|f|·λ^{−n}·Hⁿ(B_{λR}(x) ∩ M ∖ N_j).

Notation:
- Hⁿ = μHE[n] is an outer measure, so every set below has a measure and no measurability of S is needed.
- η_{x,r}(y) = r⁻¹ • (y − x) is blowUpMap x r.
- For c ∈ ℝ and T ⊆ ℝ^P, c • T := {c • z : z ∈ T}.

1. Factorization. For every y ∈ ℝ^P, η_{x,r}(y) = r⁻¹ • (y − x) = r⁻¹ • (y + (−x)). Let τ(y) := y + (−x) (translation by −x) and m(z) := r⁻¹ • z. Then η_{x,r} = m ∘ τ, so η_{x,r}(S) = m(τ(S)) (Set.image_image). Also m(T) = r⁻¹ • T for every T (Set.image_smul). Hence η_{x,r}(S) = r⁻¹ • τ(S).

2. Dilation law. Since r > 0, r⁻¹ ≠ 0. For every nonzero scalar c and every T ⊆ ℝ^P, Hⁿ(c • T) = ‖c‖₊ⁿ • Hⁿ(T) (Mathlib Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀). Geometrically: z ↦ c • z is a bijection of ℝ^P that multiplies the diameter of every set by |c|. So it carries ε-covers of T to |c|ε-covers of c • T and multiplies every sum Σ diam(Cᵢ)ⁿ by |c|ⁿ. Letting ε ↓ 0 gives the law for the Hausdorff measure, and μHE[n] is a fixed constant multiple of it. With c = r⁻¹ and T = τ(S): Hⁿ(r⁻¹ • τ(S)) = ‖r⁻¹‖₊ⁿ • Hⁿ(τ(S)).

3. Translation invariance. τ is an isometry of ℝ^P, because |τ(y) − τ(y')| = |y − y'| (Mathlib isometry_add_right (−x)). The Hausdorff measure of the image of an arbitrary set under an isometry equals that of the set (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image): isometries preserve diameters, so covers correspond with equal sums. Hence Hⁿ(τ(S)) = Hⁿ(S).

4. Constant.
- By steps 1–3, Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(S)) = ‖r⁻¹‖₊ⁿ • Hⁿ(S), where an ℝ≥0-scalar acts on ℝ≥0∞ as multiplication by its coercion (ENNReal.smul_def).
- Because r > 0, ‖r⁻¹‖ = |r⁻¹| = r⁻¹ (abs_of_pos). So ‖r⁻¹‖₊ⁿ is the nonnegative real number (r⁻¹)ⁿ, and its coercion to ℝ≥0∞ equals ENNReal.ofReal (r⁻¹ ^ n) (ENNReal.ofReal_coe_nnreal).
- Therefore Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(S)) = ENNReal.ofReal (r⁻¹ ^ n) · Hⁿ(S). ∎
proof_key_steps: Factor the blow-up as translation then dilation: η_{x,r}(S) = r⁻¹ • (S + (−x)) (Set.image_image, Set.image_smul).
Dilation law: Hⁿ(c • T) = ‖c‖₊ⁿ Hⁿ(T) for c = r⁻¹ ≠ 0 (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀).
For r > 0 the factor ‖r⁻¹‖₊ⁿ coerced to ℝ≥0∞ equals ENNReal.ofReal (r⁻¹ ^ n).

audit.reason: The one-line proposition exactly matches the prose, including arbitrary S, positive r and the ENNReal coefficient. The proof completely factors the blow-up into translation and nonzero dilation, applies the pinned measure laws without measurability assumptions, and converts the scalar correctly. It covers n = 0 and infinite measure, has no circular dependence, and provides the precise null-image fact needed by the next child.

subproblem.title: Approximate tangent spaces survive removal of a locally null set
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. Let M, M' ⊆ ℝ^P with M Borel and M' ⊆ M (M' is otherwise arbitrary). Let x ∈ ℝ^P and δ > 0 with Hⁿ((M ∖ M') ∩ B_δ(x)) = 0, where Hⁿ = μHE[n] and B_δ(x) is the open ball. Let Q be a linear subspace of ℝ^P. Suppose Q is the approximate tangent space of M at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q, meaning finrank Q = n and ∫_{η_{x,λ}(M)} f dHⁿ → ∫_Q f dHⁿ as λ ↓ 0 for all f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), where η_{x,λ}(y) = λ⁻¹(y − x). Then Q is the approximate tangent space of M' at x: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M M' : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (δ : ℝ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), MeasurableSet M → M' ⊆ M → 0 < δ → μHE[n] ((M \ M') ∩ ball x δ) = 0 → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Lemma A, steps A1–A6. It is specialized by dropping the measurability of M', which is never used. Step A4 is supplied by the sibling theorem blowup_image_measure (Submission.rsd_cmr_ir_blowUp_image_measure). The splitting of ∫_{η_{x,λ}(M)} f dHⁿ follows Simon Ch. 3, proof of Theorem 1.6 “⇒”; the approximate tangent space is Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4.

Notation:
- Hⁿ = μHE[n].
- η_λ := η_{x,λ}, with η_λ(y) = λ⁻¹(y − x) (blowUpMap x λ).
- ∫_E f dHⁿ is the Bochner integral of f for Hⁿ restricted to E; it equals 0 when f is not integrable there.
- By definition, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n E x Q means: finrank Q = n, and for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), ∫_{η_λ(E)} f dHⁿ → ∫_Q f dHⁿ as λ → 0 along 𝓝[>] 0.

1. (A1) The condition finrank Q = n is the first component of the hypothesis HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q, and it is literally the same condition for M'. It remains to prove the limit statement for M' and an arbitrary f.

2. (A2) Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ). Its topological support tsupport f is compact, hence bounded, so there is R₀ ≥ 0 with tsupport f ⊆ B̄_{R₀}(0). Since {z : f(z) ≠ 0} ⊆ tsupport f, f(z) ≠ 0 implies |z| ≤ R₀.

3. Fix λ with 0 < λ < δ/(R₀ + 1). The interval (0, δ/(R₀ + 1)) belongs to 𝓝[>] 0 because δ/(R₀ + 1) > 0.
(a) η_λ(M) is Borel. η_λ is a bijection of ℝ^P with inverse z ↦ x + λz, so η_λ(M) = {z : x + λz ∈ M} is the preimage of the Borel set M under the continuous map z ↦ x + λz.
(b) η_λ(M') ⊆ η_λ(M) because M' ⊆ M.
(c) (A4) Put Z_λ := η_λ((M ∖ M') ∩ B_δ(x)). Apply the sibling theorem blowup_image_measure with r = λ > 0 and S = (M ∖ M') ∩ B_δ(x): Hⁿ(Z_λ) = ENNReal.ofReal (λ⁻¹ ^ n) · Hⁿ((M ∖ M') ∩ B_δ(x)) = ENNReal.ofReal (λ⁻¹ ^ n) · 0 = 0.
(d) (A3) Claim: if z ∈ η_λ(M) ∖ η_λ(M') and f(z) ≠ 0, then z ∈ Z_λ.
- Write z = η_λ(y) with y ∈ M. If y ∈ M', then z ∈ η_λ(M'), which is false; so y ∈ M ∖ M'.
- From f(z) ≠ 0 and step 2, |z| ≤ R₀.
- Since z = λ⁻¹(y − x), we have y − x = λz, so |y − x| = λ|z| ≤ λR₀ ≤ λ(R₀ + 1) < δ.
- Thus y ∈ (M ∖ M') ∩ B_δ(x) and z = η_λ(y) ∈ Z_λ.
(e) (A5) By (c) and (d), for every z outside the Hⁿ-null set Z_λ (hence for Hⁿ-a.e. z ∈ ℝ^P), z ∈ η_λ(M) ∖ η_λ(M') implies f(z) = 0. Let t := η_λ(M), measurable by (a), and s := η_λ(M') ⊆ t by (b). Mathlib's setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_ae_sdiff_eq_zero (hypotheses: t null-measurable, s ⊆ t, f = 0 a.e. on t ∖ s) gives ∫_{η_λ(M)} f dHⁿ = ∫_{η_λ(M')} f dHⁿ. No integrability is needed:
- If f is integrable on t, then ∫_t f = ∫_s f + ∫_{t∖s} f, and ∫_{t∖s} f = 0 because f = 0 a.e. on t ∖ s.
- If f is not integrable on t, it is not integrable on s either: integrability on s, together with f = 0 a.e. on t ∖ s and the measurability of t, would give integrability on t (IntegrableOn.of_ae_sdiff_eq_zero). So both Bochner integrals are 0.

4. (A6) By step 3, φ(λ) := ∫_{η_λ(M)} f dHⁿ and ψ(λ) := ∫_{η_λ(M')} f dHⁿ coincide for every λ ∈ (0, δ/(R₀ + 1)), a set in 𝓝[>] 0. So φ = ψ eventually along 𝓝[>] 0. The hypothesis gives φ(λ) → ∫_Q f dHⁿ along 𝓝[>] 0, hence ψ(λ) → ∫_Q f dHⁿ along 𝓝[>] 0 (Tendsto.congr').

5. As f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ) was arbitrary, steps 1 and 4 prove HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q. ∎
proof_key_steps: finrank Q = n carries over unchanged; fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ) and R₀ ≥ 0 with f = 0 outside B̄_{R₀}(0).
For 0 < λ < δ/(R₀ + 1): η_{x,λ}(M) is Borel (preimage of M under z ↦ x + λz), and η_{x,λ}(M') ⊆ η_{x,λ}(M).
Every z ∈ η_{x,λ}(M) ∖ η_{x,λ}(M') with f(z) ≠ 0 lies in Z_λ = η_{x,λ}((M ∖ M') ∩ B_δ(x)), which is Hⁿ-null by blowup_image_measure.
setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_ae_sdiff_eq_zero: the blow-up integrals of f over η_{x,λ}(M) and η_{x,λ}(M') coincide for all such λ.
Tendsto.congr' along 𝓝[>] 0 transfers the limit ∫_Q f dHⁿ from M to M', for every f.

audit.reason: The prose and one-line Lean type agree on every hypothesis, including measurability only of M. Each proof step is justified: compact support bounds the relevant preimages, positivity gives a right-neighbourhood of zero, the declared sibling makes the exceptional image null, and the pinned integral lemma requires neither measurability of M' nor integrability. Eventual equality transfers the defining limit while preserving finrank. Applying this child to M' = R.carrier ∩ A, with sdiff_self_inter and restricted a.e. orientation data, establishes the exact selected parent through its supplied field-by-field construction.
